chapter_title: Chương 55: Khởi Hành Đến Ma Đô

segments.title: Chương 55: Khởi Hành Đến Ma Đô
segments.content:
At the three-way intersection between No. 2 High, No. 7 High, and the street of internet cafes, there was a rather large wet market.

Chen Guiliang went and bought four jin of pork, two jin of beef, and a bundle of pig liver.

If he didn't buy it in the county seat, he wouldn't be able to get any on the way home. The towns and villages only sold meat on market days. You could usually buy it in the morning, but it would definitely be gone by the afternoon.

Then he went back to the dorm to get his luggage.

He stuffed the meat he had just bought into the bucket and placed the bag with the kitten on top of it. He packed his clothes and shoes into a snakeskin bag, then put on his backpack and went to the school gate to catch the bus.

After two or three hours of jostling on the rundown bus, Chen Guiliang got off at the junction of the county road and the village road.

He carried the bucket in his left hand and the snakeskin bag in his right, and his backpack was also full of things. The whole pile was quite heavy.

He hadn't walked far before he was so tired his whole body felt sore and weak, and the kitten wouldn't stop meowing.

He remembered a certain morning in middle school, on this very same broken-down village road. It was drizzling, and the road was muddy. It was a struggle to walk in the slush, and he had to be careful not to slip and fall. The sky was still dark, making it hard to see, and on his back, he carried his schoolbag and thirty to forty jin of rice.

The rice was to be exchanged for meal tickets at school.

His sandals had been torn in the mud, and the frame of his umbrella had also been broken in a fall. Half of his body was covered in mud.

He squatted by the side of the road, so wronged he wanted to cry, watching bus after bus drive past. To save the 50-cent bus fare, he ultimately chose not to take the bus. He threw away the ruined umbrella and sandals, and continued walking to school with his schoolbag and the rice on his back.

More than twenty years had passed, but the memory was still fresh.

This broken-down village road, he had personally taken part in building it twice.

Once in elementary school, once in middle school. Every family had to contribute labor. His parents were away working, so he went with his grandmother.

The grandmother and grandson were treated quite well; they weren't made to carry stones. They just squatted by the roadside, hammering the larger stones into smaller pieces, and then carrying them to fill the potholes in the road.

When he got tired of walking, he took a rest.

Chen Guiliang whistled to tease the kitten, looked at the broken-down village road before him, and thought that he should donate some money to repair it in the future.

Pave it with cement.

By the time he reached the vicinity of his grandparents' house, it was already two in the afternoon.

It was the slack season for farming, and his maternal grandmother was by the roadside shooting the breeze with a group of old ladies. This place was something of a village intelligence hub.

"Grandma!" Chen Guiliang called out.

Realizing it was him, his grandmother walked over in pleasant surprise, "You're on break?"

"Yes, I am. I bought some meat for you."

Chen Guiliang lifted out the bag with the cat and took out two jin of pork and one jin of beef from the bucket.

Upon seeing this, the other old ladies instantly had a new topic of conversation:

"Oh my, your grandson is truly so filial, remembering to buy meat to bring back on his school break."

"Second Sister Liu, you're so fortunate."

"Last time he bought a color TV, this time he's buying meat. Being rich really makes a difference."

"..."

His grandmother beamed from ear to ear and asked, "Have you eaten?"

"I have," Chen Guiliang said.

"Come and sit at home for a bit."

"Alright."

The entire village had five administrative teams.

Each team, due to the hilly terrain, was separated into clusters of settlements.

The settlement where his grandmother lived was relatively large, with about twelve or thirteen households.

Chen Guiliang followed his grandmother to her house, and those old ladies also trailed behind, trying to extract more useless intelligence.

"Grandpa!"

"You're back."

His grandfather was still in the courtyard binding brooms. Seeing Chen Guiliang, he quickly went into the house to bring out a long stool.

Chen Guiliang casually asked, "Where's my youngest uncle?"

His grandfather said grumpily, "What else could he be doing? Playing cards, for sure."

His youngest uncle had an accident when he was in school, which left him with a slight limp in his left leg. He had no other skills, so he was still an old bachelor. As soon as he finished his farm work, he'd run off to play cards.

It wasn't gambling, just pure entertainment. A whole day of playing would only see wins or losses of two or three yuan.

Chen Guiliang sat in the courtyard, surrounded by a group of old ladies, fending off all sorts of questions.

He was a third-year high school student, yet an old lady was actually trying to play matchmaker for him!

"Guiliang, you don't have a girlfriend yet, do you? Do you know my granddaughter?"

"Who?"

"Shasha. Huang Shasha."

"I have a vague impression. She's still in middle school, isn't she?"

"She'll graduate from middle school next year. You two are such a good match."

Chen Guiliang didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

Even his grandmother chimed in, "Shasha is pretty, and very obedient."

Another old lady came up with a terrible idea, "Shasha's on break too, quick, call her over!"

Chen Guiliang really couldn't take it anymore and just wanted to escape. He quickly stood up and said, "Grandpa, Grandma, I'll be going now."

"What's the hurry?" His grandmother grabbed his hand, very enthusiastic about this matter. "Wait for Shasha to come over before you go. You two used to play together a lot when you were little. You know, Shasha's grades are also very good. Her teacher said that even if she doesn't get into No. 2 High, she'll definitely get into No. 1 High."

Chen Guiliang helplessly sat back down, waiting for his first "blind date" after being reborn.

If this could even be called a blind date.

Before long, that Huang Shasha was called over. After understanding what was going on, she was even more awkward and flustered than Chen Guiliang.

His grandfather, who had been binding brooms all this time, finally couldn't help but scold them, "You crazy old women are nuts! Why are you meddling in the affairs of a student?"

Grandfather stopped binding brooms and ran to the small shop nearby. He dragged his youngest son, who was playing cards, over to help Chen Guiliang carry his things home.

"Grandpa, Grandma, I'm leaving!"

Chen Guiliang took the opportunity to say his goodbyes.

That Huang Shasha also quickly ran off, her face flushed red.

When his youngest uncle saw that Chen Guiliang had bought a cat, he went to the kitchen and brought out half a basin of fried river shrimp, "I caught these yesterday. I sold most of them for over ten yuan, you can take what's left to feed the cat."

After speaking, his youngest uncle placed the basin, shrimp and all, into the bucket, and helped carry the snakeskin bag.

After walking for more than ten minutes, they finally arrived back at his own courtyard. Chen Guiliang handed his youngest uncle a pack of Hongtashan cigarettes.

His youngest uncle grinned, accepting it with a bit of embarrassment.

"I'll be going then," his youngest uncle said, a little anxiously.

Chen Guiliang guessed that he wanted to hurry back to play cards, so he didn't try to make him stay, just symbolically walking him a few steps.

His grandmother wasn't home again, probably off doing farm work somewhere.

Chen Guiliang let the kitten out. The cat immediately scurried away in panic, disappearing into the woodpile under the eaves.

Opening the door and going inside, Chen Guiliang found a broken bowl to use as a cat food dish. He picked out a few fried river shrimp, tossed them in, and placed the bowl by the woodpile, not bothering with it anymore.

He took out his PHS phone and tried to call Tao Chenggang, only to find that the thing had no signal in the countryside.

He might as well lie down on the bed and have a nice sleep.

When he woke up, his grandmother still hadn't returned.

Chen Guiliang ran to check the cat's food dish and found that the river shrimp had been eaten. So he threw in two more.

Then he went to the private plot next to the house, picked some vegetables his grandmother had planted, and also picked a handful of wild Gynura bicolor.

Then he washed the rice, cooked it, washed the vegetables, and cut the meat.

It was almost dark when his grandmother came home, carrying a bunch of miscellaneous scraps.

There was basically no scrap to be found in the countryside; she must have gone to the garbage dump in the next village. It was originally used to dump coal cinders from the boiler factory, but later they started dumping city garbage there, gradually piling it up into several small, spectacular hills.

The garbage dump was also Chen Guiliang's childhood playground. He could often find pencils, erasers, and books there.

His most prized spoils were a copy of *One Hundred Thousand Whys* and a copy of *The Essentials of Emei Qigong*.

He even foolishly practiced qigong according to the book for several years.

He had even invented his own method of "using qi to ward off the cold." It was too cold going to school in the winter mornings, the wind making one shiver. Chen Guiliang would use his mind to circulate his qi, moving the qi from his dantian to the shanzhong acupoint, and then channeling it to his limbs through the meridians.

After repeating this cycle for several revolutions, he would no longer feel cold.

He would even feel warm all over.

Thinking about it now, it was most likely a psychological effect.

"Grandma, I've brought the cat back," Chen Guiliang called out while stir-frying the vegetables.

"I see it!"

Grandmother stood at the entrance to the main room. The kitten poked its head out from the woodpile.

The human and the cat stared at each other.

Grandmother moved half a step, and the kitten shrank back into the woodpile to hide.

Chen Guiliang finished cooking the dishes and took one of the stir-fried pork dishes to his second uncle's house. After a few lukewarm words, he came back to eat with his grandmother.

"Grandma, I'm going to Shanghai for a competition," Chen Guiliang took out the invitation for the semi-finals.

Grandmother stared at the invitation for a long time. Although she didn't know who Han Han or Guo Xiaosi were, she still understood that this competition was a big deal.

After all, he had to go to Shanghai.

"Compete well. Do you have enough money?" his grandmother asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "I have enough."

His grandmother asked again, "When are you leaving?"

"In two days."

"Then you need to be safe. Hide your money well on the road, and don't talk too much to strangers."

"I know."

"..."

Chen Guiliang rested at home for a day, and on the next, he went to the city to buy a train ticket, and also a decent suitcase.

He couldn't possibly carry a snakeskin bag to Shanghai.

When he arrived at the private server operation command center, Chen Guiliang didn't see Tao Chenggang.

Only after asking did he learn that CEO Tao had gone to the surrounding cities and counties to promote the game in internet cafes.

Yang Yuhui said, "The internet cafe promotion has been very effective. The peak concurrent user count has already surpassed ten thousand. By the way, there's some news about the special campaign."

"What news?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Yang Yuhui said, "The focus is mainly on cracking down on pirated software manufacturers, so it hasn't been that intense online. But there are exceptions. Over in E Province, they're cracking down both online and offline. I heard some people who run private servers have already been detained and fined."

Chen Guiliang laughed.

From the second year private servers appeared all the way to twenty years later, E Province was always the most active place for them!

Many private server dens were located in E Province.

There were even a few years when Shanda specifically targeted E Province, maintaining a long-term strategic partnership with the province's cyber police.

That night, Chen Guiliang stayed at his second cousin's house and made calls to both Bian Guanyue and Tao Xue.

Early the next morning, he took a train straight to Rongcheng.

His second cousin's wife, Lin Chunhong, was truly a good and virtuous wife. She had specially boiled twenty eggs for Chen Guiliang.
